question: The Henry Dunant Centre for Humanitarian Dialogue has taken part in various peace negotiations in regions of strategic interest for the Union and, as published on the organisation’s online transparency register, it receives significant funding from the EU. It is therefore surprising that there is a lack of easily accessible public information detailing how the EU funds are used.

In view of this, we would like some information on the EU funding this centre received between 2004 and 2024: the origin of the funds and the annual allocation, as well as a detailed breakdown of how those funds are used and the activities they finance.
answer: From 2007 to 2024, the Henry Dunant Centre for Humanitarian Dialogue received a total of EUR 57.5 million for projects supporting conflict prevention and peace or stabilisation processes, for example through mediation (1).

Pursuant to Article 38(3)(d) of Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2018/1046 (2), some information on transactions may not be published in cases where disclosure risks threatening the rights and freedoms of the persons or entities concerned as protected by the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union.
In the annex, the Honorable Member will find the details on funding and the related financed activities which can be published in line with Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2018/1046. See annex: Annex
There were no contracts with the Henry Dunant Centre for Humanitarian Dialogue before 2007. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex%3A32018R1046
